The task: I'm a model inside a sleep tracking app. The app displays my returned remark directly under tonight's sleep numbers (one line). I need to return only JSON: {"remark":"..."}

Component analysis: The remark shown under sleep numbers is a 小字備註 (small note): "一句會改變旁邊數字或清單怎麼讀的事實；沒有就留空" — one fact that changes how the nearby number or list is read; if none, leave empty.

So the remark should be one fact that changes how tonight's numbers should be read. Not a coaching sentence, not encouragement, not advice. Just a fact.

Data: Time in bed 7h50m, asleep 6h20m, took 48 minutes to fall asleep, woke 3 times; user's goal is 7h asleep. Past 7 days average time to fall asleep: 15 minutes.

Which fact changes how the number reads? The asleep time is 6h20m vs goal 7h — that's already visible presumably (the numbers shown). The fact that changes reading: tonight's sleep onset was 48 minutes vs 7-day average 15 minutes — i.e., falling asleep took much longer than usual. That's a fact that changes how the "asleep 6h20m" reads — the shortfall is mostly from longer sleep onset, not more night waking.

The note should be one sentence, a fact, using full-width punctuation. Format examples: "醬汁另計／約 40 秒錄音聽不清楚／（空）".

So something like: "入睡耗時 48 分鐘，比近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。" Or "入睡花了 48 分鐘，近 7 天平均 15 分鐘。"

Hmm, but "入睡花了 48 分鐘" — is that already on screen? The listed data includes all tonight's data: in bed, asleep, onset time, wakings. The app shows tonight's sleep numbers; we don't know exactly which are displayed. The remark should be a fact that changes how the numbers read. The comparison to the 7-day average is the key fact not otherwise visible: falling asleep took 48 minutes vs usual 15.

Keep it short, one line. Traditional Chinese, Taiwan usage. Use full-width punctuation. Numbers with unit: 48 分鐘. Range/en dash for ranges.

Option: "入睡耗時為近 7 天平均的 3 倍。" That changes the reading: the sleep-onset was unusually long.

Or: "入睡 48 分鐘，明顯高於近 7 天平均 15 分鐘。" "明顯" is an interpretation; the note should be a fact. A comparison is a fact.

Simplest: "入睡 48 分鐘，較近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。" One sentence, fact, changes reading of tonight's numbers (shortfall mostly due to sleep onset).

Should I mention the goal? The goal (7h) is likely displayed already as the target. The asleep 6h20m vs 7h goal shortfall = 40 min; the extra sleep onset (48−15=33 min) plus 3 wakings accounts. But the note should be ONE fact, one sentence.

I'll go with: "入睡 48 分鐘，比近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。"

Alternatively "入睡時間 48 分鐘，近 7 天平均 15 分鐘。" That presents both figures without computing. The 範例 style for 小字備註 is very terse: "醬汁另計". So terse: "入睡較近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。"

I think "入睡 48 分鐘，比近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。" is good — one line, fact, changes reading.

Return only JSON.{"remark":"入睡 48 分鐘，比近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。"}

parsed.remark: 入睡 48 分鐘，比近 7 天平均多 33 分鐘。
